newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia c.bank sells HRK162 mln bills, rates flat.
newsitem.headline: Croatia c.bank sells HRK162 mln bills, rates flat.

text.p: Croatia's central bank sold 162 million kuna worth of its liquidity bills to the banking sector an auction on Wednesday.
The volume of newly issued bills rose from last week's 131 million, with the 35- and 91-day rates unchanged at 7.0 and 8.5 percent, respectively.
The interest for the central bank paper has been on a slight increase because commercial banks use them as collateral for Lombard funds, granted at 9.5 percent for a maximum of 12 working days.
They currently have over 136 million kuna in outstanding Lombard funds, the bank said.

"Today's new borrowing is about 10-11 million but it will increase. We have announcements of large payments," an official told Reuters, adding this was due to a payment of the 1996 profit tax by the banks' corporate clients.

Monday's statutory reserves drained a total of 3.39 billion kuna from the banking sector, or 44.3 million kuna more than under a previous fortnightly obligation. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
